results.description: Controller vx_max 0.5 -> 2.0, smoother left at 0.5
results.rationale: Controller now plans 4x faster than the chain delivers, and the prediction horizon (56 * 0.05 * 2.0 = 5.6 m) far overruns the 1.5 m costmap radius.
new_findings: NAV2_HORIZON_EXCEEDS_COSTMAP|MPPI prediction horizon reaches 5.600 m beyond the 1.500 m local costmap radius
NAV2_VELOCITY_OVERDECLARED|Controller declares maximum forward velocity 4.00x the downstream smoother limit

results.description: Speed raised coherently on BOTH controller and smoother, 0.5 -> 2.0
results.rationale: A 4x speed increase with no change to braking, sensor range, or costmap size. The limit-coherence check cannot see it because the two declarations still agree. Only the horizon rule catches it, and only because MPPI happens to declare a prediction horizon. Stopping distance quadruples and nothing in EAL models that.
new_findings: NAV2_HORIZON_EXCEEDS_COSTMAP|MPPI prediction horizon reaches 5.600 m beyond the 1.500 m local costmap radius

results.description: DWB speed raised coherently, 0.26 -> 2.0 on controller and smoother
results.rationale: Same 8x speed increase on the DWB stack. DWB declares no prediction horizon, so the horizon rule does not apply and EAL is entirely silent. This is the clearest demonstration of the envelope's limit: a coherent, dangerous change on a controller without a horizon is invisible.

results.description: Local costmap shrunk 3x3 m -> 1x1 m
results.rationale: 1.4 m of prediction against a 0.5 m radius. The planner reasons about space it has no map data for.
new_findings: NAV2_HORIZON_EXCEEDS_COSTMAP|MPPI prediction horizon reaches 1.400 m beyond the 0.500 m local costmap radius

results.description: Sensor marking range obstacle_max_range 2.5 -> 0.4 m (local costmap)
results.rationale: Obstacles beyond 0.4 m are discarded before reaching the costmap (obstacle_layer.cpp:552), so the robot cannot brake for what it cannot see. EAL extracts this value but no check consumes it. A severe hazard that is fully present in the config and still invisible.

results.description: Inflation radius 0.70 -> 0.05 m
results.rationale: The inflation layer is what keeps planned paths away from obstacles rather than grazing them. At 0.05 m the margin is below the costmap resolution, so paths may be planned essentially in contact with obstacles. EAL extracts inflation_radius and relates it to nothing, so the change is invisible.

results.description: controller_frequency 20 Hz -> 2 Hz
results.rationale: Control period grows from 50 ms to 500 ms, adding 0.45 m of travel at 1 m/s before the next command. Extracted as a timing parameter, unchecked.

results.description: Local costmap update_frequency 5 Hz -> 0.5 Hz
results.rationale: Obstacle data becomes up to 2 s stale, so at 0.5 m/s the robot may act on a picture of the world a metre out of date. The value is extracted and typed as a timing parameter, but no check relates costmap freshness to the speed the robot is allowed to travel, so nothing fires.

results.description: Smoother max_decel -2.5 -> -0.4, controller left at -3.0
results.rationale: Controller assumes 7.5x the braking the chain will deliver. This is the case the check was built for, at an exaggerated ratio.
new_findings: NAV2_ACCEL_OVERDECLARED|Controller declares linear deceleration limit 7.50x the downstream smoother limit

results.description: Braking weakened coherently on both sides, 3.0/2.5 -> 0.4
results.rationale: Stopping distance from 0.5 m/s grows from 0.05 m to 0.31 m, over 6x, and the two declarations agree perfectly. Coherent and dangerous.

results.description: wz_max written in deg/s instead of rad/s (1.9 -> 108.9)
results.rationale: Caught, but as a 54x over-declaration rather than as a unit error. Right alarm, wrong diagnosis — record it as a partial detection.
new_findings: NAV2_VELOCITY_OVERDECLARED|Controller declares maximum angular velocity 54.45x the downstream smoother limit

results.description: Angular limits converted to deg/s on both sides consistently
results.rationale: A consistent unit error is arithmetically coherent. EAL has no notion of a plausible magnitude for a quantity, so nothing fires.

results.description: ax_min deleted from the controller block
results.rationale: One side of a coherence comparison has vanished. EAL was asked to check that limits agree and can no longer do so for this role, which is the definition of UNKNOWN. If it instead stays silent, that is the TD-2 failure mode returning at finer grain.

results.description: Entire velocity_smoother section removed
results.rationale: Documented as inapplicable rather than unknown: a stack legitimately may not run the smoother. Listed so the decision stays visible and arguable.

results.description: vx_max declared twice in the same block with different values
results.rationale: YAML silently keeps the last duplicate key, so the file says 0.5 to a human reader and 3.0 to the parser. Any tool claiming to review configuration must not quietly adopt one reading. Expected UNKNOWN; a silent result here would be a serious defect.
new_findings: NAV2_HORIZON_EXCEEDS_COSTMAP|MPPI prediction horizon reaches 8.400 m beyond the 1.500 m local costmap radius
NAV2_VELOCITY_OVERDECLARED|Controller declares maximum forward velocity 6.00x the downstream smoother limit

results.description: Second controller plugin block with contradictory limits
results.rationale: The importer takes the first plugin entry that resolves and never looks at the second, so a contradictory alternative controller is unexamined.

results.description: batch_size 2000 -> 1000 (compute budget, not a safety limit)
results.rationale: Sampling budget. Any finding here is a false positive.

results.description: visualize true -> false (debug output only)
results.rationale: Debug flag. Any finding here is a false positive.

results.description: A comment line added inside the controller block
results.rationale: Whitespace and comments must not affect a deterministic result.

results.description: Unrecognised controller plugin
results.rationale: No validated role mapping exists for this plugin, so none of its motion limits can be extracted and none of the coherence checks can run. Guessing a mapping from familiar-looking parameter names would produce a confident result with nothing behind it, so the honest output is UNKNOWN rather than a clean pass.

results.description: Unmodelled extra parameter added to the controller block
results.rationale: Real configs carry many parameters EAL does not model. Flagging every one would make the tool unusable; silence here is correct, not a gap.

results.description: Smoother claims 100 m/s^2 braking capability
results.rationale: Roughly 10 g of braking, physically absurd for a wheeled robot. Because the controller is now the conservative side, the only thing EAL says is a strict-only informational item. It has no notion of physical plausibility.

results.description: Zero modelled actuation delay asserted alongside a 2 Hz control loop
results.rationale: The model asserts no actuation delay while the loop runs at 500 ms. EAL extracts both numbers and never relates them.
